messages.author: 5900eadecec2d82d
messages.subject: Strip transects in Distance
parts:
Hi Tim,

My reply below. I'm forwarding this to the distance-sampling list as your
question seemed to be of general interest.

On Fri, 10 Dec 1999 08:57:03 -0800, Tim Gerrodette wrote:

> >Len,
> >
> >I'm planning to use Distance in a turtle workshop next spring where I
> >think much of the data will be strip transects. Obviously estimating
> >ESW is not an issue, but Distance will estimate density and variance,
> >etc.
> >
> >My plan for the data format is to enter, in place of perp distance, the
> >(half) width of the strip transect for each sighting. Then in Distance,
> >I will specify a uniform DF with 0 adjustments. I think this should
> >work to analyze strip transect data. A special problem arises in the
> >case of a transect with no sightings. This doesn't cause a problem for
> >line transects, but in the case of strip transects the area covered on
> >that transect with no sightings will not be counted in the area
> >surveyed, so the estimated density will be incorrect. My solution is to
> >specify a half-width for this transect, but then to give a cluster size
> >of 0. this triggers a warning, naturally, but the results seem to be
> >OK.
> >
> >Do you have other experience using Distance with strip transects, or do
> >you have other suggestions for how to adapt Distance in this case?
> >
> >I thought of posting this message to the Distance discussion group, but
> >decided it was probably not of sufficient general interest. If you
> >think it is, and that others may benefit from what I suggested or from
> >your comments in response, please feel free to post this message in any
> >format you feel is useful.
> >
> >Tim

You're quite right on your approach to setting up the model definition:
specify uniform key function under Detection Function | Models, and then in
|Adjustment terms, choose Manual selection with 0 adjustment parameters.
Distance will then assume probability of detection of 1 between 0 and the
truncation distance.

I would do the other bits differently from you however:

Regarding data entry, it does not matter what distances you enter for the
observations, so long as they are between 0 and the truncation distance
(inclusive). The distances will have no effect on the analysis (other than
distances > truncation distance will be truncated). Also, you do not have to
enter "dummy" observations on strips with no observations; just treat them as
normal (ie leave the columns in the observation data layer blank). This last
point is important.

Regarding analysis, I would define a data filter with right truncation
distance set to be the width of the strip. Using this data filter and the
Uniform/No adjustments model definition you should get the correct results.
Obviously, GOF, AIC etc should be ignored as you are not really fitting a
detection function, but density, abundance, variance, etc will be correct (I
realize you knew this already, but thought other distance-sampling readers
may not).

When writing Distance 3.5 I almost added a 4th survey type "Strip transect"
to the setup project wizard. Choosing this would have caused Distance to not
create a "Distance" field in the observation layer (you would use the cluster
size field to denote the number of objects seen), and would have grayed out
the "Detection Function" tab in Model Definition (using Uniform/No
adjustments in all analyses). However I ran out of time as you would ideally
want to modify the analysis engine as well as the interface to give
appropriate output. If anyone thinks its worthwhile for future versions let
me know. I will certainly try to put something in the Distance 4 online
manual about strip transects in any case.

Good luck with your workshop - I hope the turtles enjoy it! ;)
All the best,

- Len

messages.author: 5900eadecec2d82d
messages.subject: Re: Strip transects in Distance
parts:
More on strip transects. Ignore if they don't interest you!

On Mon, 13 Dec 1999 14:23:00 -0800, Tim Gerrodette wrote:

> >Len:
> >
> >Thanks for the reply about using strip transects in Distance. I see
> >that I was mistaken about having to enter dummy values for strip
> >transects with no sightings. I was sure that I had tried this and found
> >that such transects were ignored unless a dummy was present, but clearly
> >they are not.

No problem.

> >I see that Distance will assume a strip width equal to the specified
> >right truncation value, or, if this is not given, to the largest
> >perpendicular distance recorded. I think this is somewhat of a
> >limitation for strip transects, as noted below.
> >
> >I think it would be a good idea to include strip transects as an option
> >in future versions of Distance. Despite the known advantages of line
> >and point transects, there are still some situations where perpendicular
> >distance either cannot be measured or is not useful. Strip transects
> >continue to have some very limited use.

I quite agree - strip transects (and quadrat methods) defiantly have their
uses, for example in populations at high densities, where you can "afford" to
do a complete census within the narrow strip where detection is certain and
ignore all observations outside the strip. Distance sampling, on the other
hand, tends to be more useful where populations are sparser or are hard to
detect, so that each observation is more "precious". Then the cost (in
precision) of estimating the detection function is outweighed by the benefit
of the extra observations. There's also the logistical issue of being able
to measure distances, which you mention.

> >In strip transects, it might
> >also be useful to allow different transects to have different widths
> >(this was the reason I wanted to specify strip width in the data, not by
> >using right truncation).

This is a good idea that I had not thought of. Presumably, you grouped all
transects with the same strip width into the same "stratum" within Distance
and then specified in the Model Definition | Level of Estimation boxes to
estimate detection function by stratum.

> > Here's an example of the latter: a transect
> >down the middle of a narrow river which can be covered visually from
> >bank to bank, but different sections of the river (different transects)
> >have different widths. As I understand it, the present software does not
> >allow this situation.

No, it doesn't, apart from using the method you described above. I'll put it
on the list for D4 (doesn't guarantee it'll get done, but at least it's on
the list!). I'm also thinking about how to implement an elegant interface to
allow users to enter and analyze surveys that involve strip transects on some
lines and distance sampling on others (following your example, this could be
where the protocol calls for strip transects where the river is < 100m wide,
distance sampling where > 100m wide. The only problem here is that animal
density is rarely constant as you go across a river, so putting a survey line
right down the centre is a bad idea for the distance sampling survey.
However this is a different issue and could be addressed in all sorts of
ways...)

- Len

> >All the best,
> >
> >Tim
